sovereign_country.strategic_role: 支持全中文章程、传统华人客群离岸家族信托常驻地

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Eco-Friendly Beechwood Turning of Non-Toxic Sensory Toddler Toys

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law foundation with local statutory overlay and customary law elements; unitary national system)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER-Plus)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended by the International Companies Amendment Act 2021); Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007; International Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2022; SIFA AML/CFT Directive 2023; Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2008.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each shareholder, director, and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public / Commissioner of Oaths in country of issue
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by competent authority (e.g., state government in the US) or consular legalization by a Samoan diplomatic/consular mission if the issuance state is not an Apostille Party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter and proof of source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized by the issuing bank; apostille or consular legalization as required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified corporate extract and register of directors for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille by the home country competent authority; if non-Hague, consular legalization through Samoa's diplomatic mission

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All applicants, directors, shareholders, and UBOs must be screened against the UN Consolidated List, US OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, UK HMT sanctions list, Interpol Red Notices, and the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit's domestic watchlist before onboarding. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) require senior management approval, enhanced due diligence, and continuous monitoring under section 10 of the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007. All screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) eServices Company Registry Portal — https://www.sifa.ws
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be in Latin/Roman characters and may include Arabic numerals and limited punctuation. If the client uses a Chinese-character or other non-Latin name, a precise Latin-script transliteration must be filed first and takes legal precedence; the non-Latin translation may be approved only as a secondary trademark or reserved name after the Latin name is cleared.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of rejection, annexing consent letters, trademark certificates, or other curative evidence. If the Registrar affirms the refusal, the filer may apply for administrative review by the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 21 days; a final ministerial decision must be issued within 30 days. Name clearances not used within 30 days lapse, but a fresh application is permitted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A standalone virtual office is not permissible as the registered office; a physical address in Samoa is mandatory and is ordinarily maintained by a licensed registered agent. The company may use remote or virtual business addresses abroad for commercial correspondence, but such addresses cannot replace the statutory Samoan physical registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 10% annual likelihood for a low-risk, non-financial trading entity; 15% likelihood in the first year if the registered agent changes or a sanctions/AML alert is triggered)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the International Companies (Fees) Regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation registration fee for International Company (authorized capital below USD 100,000)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) / Registrar of International Companies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Schedule of Fees under the International Companies Act 1987

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year registered agent and registered office retainer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark / registered agent service agreement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of memorandum and articles, UBO register, and KYC file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark / fixed legal fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille/consular legalization, and international courier dispatch
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public / Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) / courier service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Samoa Diplomatic and Consular Services Fees Regulations / actual disbursements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory stamp fee for issuance of certificate of incorporation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), ss. 7–12 (incorporation), s. 14 (registered office), ss. 29–40 (directors and officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA), Apia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of an International Company (Form IC-1) and Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed; an International Company may issue shares in any currency and defer payment of unpaid amounts. No statutory escrow account or compulsory capital deposit is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscription and allotment of the initial 10,000 ordinary shares of no par value be and is hereby ratified and accepted, and the register of members be updated accordingly. RESOLVED FURTHER that the premises at [registered office address], Apia, Samoa, be and are hereby adopted as the registered office of the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER that [first-director-name] be and is hereby appointed the first director, and [company-secretary-name] be and is hereby appointed the first secretary, each to act for the Company's benefit until lawfully replaced. RESOLVED FURTHER that the director and secretary be authorized to execute all statutory registrations and open bank accounts as may be required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) — Registration Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the SIFSA-approved platform; reserve the proposed name for 90 days. Prepare and execute the memorandum and articles of association and obtain signed consents of the initial subscriber, directors, and secretary.
required_dossiers: Declaration of bona fide intention by subscriber
Consent to act as director and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as misleading or prohibited, the applicant may resubmit a revised name through Form IC-2; no hearing is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form IC-1 and the executed memorandum/articles to the Registrar, together with certified identity documents, evidence of registered office address, and the prescribed government fee. The Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation upon verifying compliance with the International Companies Act 1987.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of passport or national identification for subscriber and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Registrar may issue an amendment note identifying defects; the applicant may file corrected Form IC-1 and supplementary documents within 14 days. A refusal is appealable to the Supreme Court of Samoa.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Adoption of Corporate Governance Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 21 days after incorporation, convene the first board meeting to pass the pro-forma first board resolution, ratify share subscription, adopt the registered office, appoint officers, approve the common seal if desired, and authorize opening of bank accounts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum cannot be obtained, the sole director may act by written resolution; alternatively, SIFSA accepts a later board meeting date upon filing of a notice of postponement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Filing and Annual Levy Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File registered office particulars with SIFSA and pay the international company annual levy. Maintain the registered office and corporate records at the designated Samoan address as required under section 14 of the International Companies Act 1987.
required_dossiers: Form IC-3 notice of registered office
Copy of registered office lease or service agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late payment attracts interest and penalties; the remedy is to remit the overdue levy and file all outstanding documents promptly to avoid administrative strike-off.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Licence and Industrial Operation Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) — Business Licence Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Business Licence under the Business Licence Act 1998 to manufacture eco-friendly beechwood sensory toddler toys. Attach the certificate of incorporation, factory details, product safety testing for non-toxic finishes, and waste management plan.
required_dossiers: Certified identity documents of director or proprietor
Site lease or land title evidence
Factory production and waste management plan
Product conformity certificate for toy safety (EN71 / ASTM F963)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: MCIL may issue a written query requesting supplemental safety or environmental information; the applicant may submit a response, or may request administrative review by the Minister within 15 days of any refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA/MNRE) and Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Undertake environmental impact assessment registration and obtain the EIA clearance certificate from PUMA. Secure a fire safety certificate for the premises and workplace health clearance from the Labour inspectorate before commencing manufacturing operations.
required_dossiers: EIA application form and screening report
Fire safety plan and building evacuation diagram
Building occupancy or structural load inspection report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: PUMA may require a full EIA report if the facility is classified higher tier; FESA may order remedial fire-safety works. The applicant may revise and resubmit the required documentation and appeal final refusal through the PUMA review committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) — Business Licence Office

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 — EIA Registration / Preliminary Environmental Assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet Samoa water quality standards; airborne particulates and VOCs shall be controlled by dust extraction and low-VOC water-based finishes; workplace noise shall not exceed 55 dB(A) at the site boundary; solid waste segregation and hazardous waste removal shall comply with the Waste Management Act 2005.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA) after inspection of means of escape, extinguishers, and alarm systems; structural load inspection certificate from MCIL Building Inspectorate; occupational health clearance under the Labour and Employment Act 2013 covering workshop safety, dust control, and child protection barriers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (Samoa Tax Administration), Apia, Samoa, headed by the Commissioner of Inland Revenue within the Ministry of Finance framework; official tax and customs portal: https://www.mof.gov.ws.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Samoa International Company (IC): (1) engage a SIFA-licensed registered agent (trustee or corporate service provider) to incorporate under the International Companies Act 2009; (2) the Registrar of the Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) issues a Company Registration Number (CRN) within 1-3 business days, which serves as the sole tax reference number because the IC is statutorily tax-exempt and no separate TIN or VAGST number is issued for offshore operations; (3) file the statutory tax-exemption declaration with the Ministry for Revenue to obtain a Certificate of Tax Exemption, which evidences exemption to banks, customs, and payment rails such as Amazon Pay and Stripe; (4) if the IC nevertheless undertakes domestic Samoan taxable supplies (normally prohibited by the ring-fence), apply for a standard TIN and, above the WST 100,000 turnover threshold, compulsory VAGST registration; (5) if the IC employs staff in Samoa, register as a PAYE employer; (6) maintain a registered office and licensed agent in Apia at all times for tax and regulatory correspondence; constitutional documents may lawfully be drafted wholly in Chinese, supporting the traditional Chinese offshore family-trust client base.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: The Samoa International Company is ring-fenced from the national tax net, being exempt from income tax, Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST), stamp duty, and all other Samoan taxes, duties, and fees on income, capital, distributions, and instruments arising outside Samoa; the exemption is statute-backed and government-guaranteed for 20 years from incorporation, provided the IC does not carry on prohibited domestic business (transactions with Samoan residents, local asset ownership, or local-source revenue); the IC is additionally exempt from exchange-control and banking-licence requirements, is not subject to entity-level taxation in Samoa, and has no economic-substance, local-director, or minimum-capital obligation, making it eligible as a passive holding and e-commerce export vehicle for ISIC 3240 baby Montessori wooden blocks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Statutory elections and mechanisms: (i) formal election to activate and evidence the IC Act 2009 tax-exemption through a declaration filed with the Registrar, producing a Certificate of Tax Exemption required by banks, customs, and online payment settlement providers; (ii) shareholder-level pass-through election by non-resident beneficial owners, so the IC is treated as transparent in the beneficial-owner jurisdiction, with Samoa imposing no withholding tax, CFC charge, or exit tax on such electing shareholders; (iii) voluntary VAGST registration election for a non-exempt Samoan trading subsidiary to recover input credits on local freight, warehousing, and utility costs, whereas the exempt IC itself cannot charge or reclaim VAGST; (iv) no check-the-box classification regime exists under Samoan domestic law, and Samoa provides no domestic anti-hybrid election because the IC's full exemption eliminates any Samoan-side hybrid mismatch.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) enacted under the VAGST Act 1993, as amended; administered by the Ministry for Revenue.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 per annum in taxable supplies (compulsory VAGST registration for domestic suppliers); voluntary registration permitted below the threshold, and zero-rated exporters may register to obtain input-credit refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal-invoice clearance, government e-invoicing API, or digital-stamping mandate is currently in force in Samoa; registered VAGST suppliers must issue a compliant tax invoice containing supplier and recipient names, both TINs, serial number, date, supply description, and VAGST amount within 28 days of supply; export consignments are declared electronically through the ASYCUDA World customs clearance platform using the Export Declaration form; exporters must retain electronic records, including Amazon Pay and Stripe settlement reports, for a minimum of 5 years for audit control purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods (including beechwood, non-toxic Montessori sensory toddler blocks under ISIC 3240) are zero-rated under the VAGST Act 1993 where: (i) the goods are physically exported from Samoa within 28 days of supply or such further period as the Commissioner approves; (ii) the exporter holds a valid electronic export declaration in ASYCUDA World; (iii) payment is received in foreign currency from a non-resident, including settlement proceeds remitted through Amazon Pay or Stripe; and (iv) the complete export-documentation bundle is retained. The Samoa IC operates under pure tax-exempt-zone treatment: it charges no VAGST on export sales, and any input VAGST embedded in local costs (port handling, Apia warehousing) is not creditable; a non-exempt or voluntarily registered exporter would instead claim input-credit refunds via periodic VAGST returns.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: ASYCUDA World electronic Export Declaration (Customs Export Declaration)
Commercial invoice / supplier's tax invoice cross-referenced to the export declaration
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing port of loading in Samoa and foreign destination
Foreign-currency inward remittance certificate (bank MT103/MT950 or Amazon Pay/Stripe settlement statement evidencing receipt in WS Tala equivalent)
Packing list and, if preferential tariff treatment is claimed, certificate of origin
Copy of the IC Certificate of Tax Exemption evidencing exempt-zone status to customs and banks
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Retrospective customs and VAGST audits may cover up to 5 tax years, with full document-production powers over e-commerce books and records. If the export substantiation file is incomplete, zero-rating is disregarded and VAGST is clawed back at 15% on the full invoice value, plus statutory late-payment penalties and monthly interest on unpaid tax. Fraudulent export claims (false export declarations, fictitious foreign remittances, or sham exemption certificates) constitute tax evasion under the VAGST Act 1993 and the Income Tax Act 1974, exposing directors and officers to criminal fines per offence and imprisonment of up to 5 years, automatic revocation of the IC's tax-exempt status, and retrospective taxation of all previously exempt income and distributions; breach of the domestic ring-fence (supplies to Samoan residents or local-source revenue) triggers full clawback of the 20-year exemption guarantee.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), Apia, Samoa - sole monetary authority and foreign exchange controller under the Exchange Control Act 1975 and Exchange Control Regulations 1976; CBS licenses authorized dealer banks and supervises the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2018 (AMLCFT Act 2018).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is not freely convertible offshore. Current-account transactions are liberally approved by authorized dealers upon documentary evidence; capital-account transactions require CBS approval unless an International Company (IC) exchange-control exemption applies. An International Company incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 is exempt from Exchange Control Act restrictions in respect of all non-WST denominated dealings, provided it maintains no resident-linked WST account, transacts no business in Samoa with residents, and channels all equity, trade proceeds and dividends through external USD accounts. Dividend and profit remittances to non-resident shareholders from the IC's approved USD operational account are unrestricted and require no CBS permit; any incidental conversion of USD dividends into WST for onshore disbursement requires an authorized dealer exchange-control form and CBS post-transaction verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the CBS Exchange Control Notice to Exporters and regulation 8 of the Exchange Control Regulations 1976, exporters must receive full payment for exported goods within six months from date of shipment; foreign-currency export proceeds received by a resident must be surrendered to an authorized dealer within 30 days of receipt or be credited only to a CBS-approved foreign-currency account. For the Samoan International Company (ISIC 3240 baby Montessori wooden blocks exporter), a standing CBS exemption applies to external sales: the IC may retain 100 percent of export proceeds in its offshore-class USD account with an authorized dealer and has no WST surrender ratio because the export transaction is concluded with non-resident buyers in foreign currency. The authorized dealer reports all external receipts and account movements to CBS under the monthly exchange-control return.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD External Operational Account - International Company exempt class

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. Stripe and Amazon Pay do not list Samoa (WS) as a supported payout jurisdiction, and mainstream offshore EMIs (Wise, Mercury, Payoneer, dLocal) generally decline direct onboarding of a Samoan-incorporated IC as a non-resident beneficiary. Viable legal architecture: retain the Samoan IC as merchant of record, direct Amazon Pay/Stripe payout receivables to a licensed third-party payment transmitter or sponsored U.S./Singapore merchant account, and remit onward by SWIFT MT103 to the IC's USD account at a CBS-licensed authorized dealer. A direct EMI-held account is feasible only via an Asia-Pacific digital bank or a U.S. state money transmitter that accepts WS-IC documentation; however, single-EMI concentration is inadvisable given payment-freeze and FATCA/CRS reporting exposure. Treasury rule: the CBS-licensed USD account must remain the anchor liquidity rail; EMI balances should never exceed 30 days of operating liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permitted for non-resident directors of an International Company; no Samoan statute mandates physical landfall in Apia. In practice, authorized dealers require: (a) a video-conference compliance interview of the signatory and every beneficial owner above 10 percent; (b) certified/notarized passport copies and original verified identification presented to the Samoan registered agent; (c) a physical in-branch visit only where the UBO presents negative verification or a PEP/heightened-risk flag; and (d) the registered agent's signed identification certificate under the AMLCFT Act 2018. Where the bank's internal policy insists on a face-to-face meeting, the director may attend the nearest BSP/Samoa Commercial Bank branch or the Samoa consulate in their country of residence for notarial verification, with the compliance officer participating by video link.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face onboarding of a non-resident-owned International Company with no previous Samoan banking track record
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies of all directors and beneficial owners; utility bill or bank statement of each UBO dated within three months; bank reference letters from the UBO's primary banking relationship; notarized Certificate of Good Standing issued by the Samoan Registrar of International Companies; board resolution resolving to open and operate the account; register of members and certificate of incumbency; signed source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declaration; apostilled incorporation documents; registered agent compliance opinion and KYC identification certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity e-commerce exposure with Amazon Pay and Stripe settlement flows originating from multiple foreign jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed AML questionnaire describing the product line (beechwood, non-toxic Montessori sensory blocks, ISIC 3240/NAICS 339930); Amazon seller storefront verification and seller ID; Stripe and Amazon settlement statements matching forecast revenue and transaction counts; FBA shipment receipts and customs declarations; order-to-cash flow diagram; ERP/invoicing log; risk logic showing no collection accounts in prohibited jurisdictions; undertaking to notify the bank of any material change in payment channel or product mix within 10 business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound receipts from third-party payment facilitators (Payoneer, dLocal, Windcave) without direct customer invoices on the face of the MT103
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade file: purchase orders from Amazon Marketplace or wholesale distributors; commercial invoices; air waybills or ocean bills of lading; Samoa Customs export certificates; warehouse receipts from the U.S./EU fulfillment centers; facilitator payout statements; underlying e-commerce seller agreements; reconciliation table linking each clearing batch to the corresponding sale; bank-confirmed FX contract tickets where conversion arises.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee shareholder or trust-layer structure obscuring beneficial ownership of the International Company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: For trusts: trust deed, trustee board resolution, written verification of settlor and protector identity, source-of-wealth statement for trust corpus, and certified extract from the register of beneficial owners. For corporate nominees: nominee agreement, declaration of trust over shares, ultimate parent corporate registry extract, and a group ownership chart signed by the registered agent. The documented chain must satisfy the Samoan Beneficial Ownership Register requirements administered by the Registrar.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shell-risk screening triggered by absence of local economic substance (tax-exempt zone entity with management abroad)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Annual economic substance declaration filed with the Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL); registered agent lease and service agreement; books and records physically maintained in Samoa; annual financial statements lodged locally; minutes of board decisions held through the Apia registered office; evidence that the Samoan IC only carries on external business in compliance with the International Companies Act 1987; nil reliance on domestic tax exemptions to disguise unregulated trading.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholder capital injection: remitter issues SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 to the bank's U.S. correspondent) in favor of the IC's USD account at the Samoan authorized dealer. Field 70 should state 'INVEST // CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION EQUITY'; the underlying purpose code follows the CBS/authorized dealer capital-account classification for 'other investment - equity injection into an exempt international company'. Verification bundle required by the receiving bank: board resolution approving share allotment; updated register of members; beneficial ownership declaration; source-of-funds certificate of the shareholder; and CBS exemptions letter or delegated-authority acknowledgment. For injections exceeding the CBS-published delegated approval threshold, the authorized dealer must submit the exchange-control application form to CBS before crediting; standing IC exemption usually converts this to a post-credit compliance file. Use only USD-clearing corridors (BSP's designated New York correspondent is the standard route); no WST conversion is permitted on inward foreign-currency equity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For supplier trade payments (beechwood lumber, non-toxic lacquers, packaging): (a) open-account purchases below the authorized-dealer threshold are cleared by direct SWIFT MT103 against pro-forma invoice, packing list, air waybill or bill of lading and commercial contract; (b) larger shipments use an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (MT700) issued by the Samoan IC's bank in favor of the supplier, with settlement via MT202/MT103 against conforming documents; (c) periodic service fees to Amazon/Stripe and fulfillment centers are paid as batch host-to-host MT101-Initiated customer credit transfers from the USD operational account; (d) every outward disbursement must be mapped to the CBS balance-of-payments purpose code and retained in the bank's transaction-monitoring system. The IC must not direct settlement to a resident Samoan supplier account unless that supplier is separately licensed for foreign-currency dealings.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/WST deliverable foreign-exchange forward contracts (tenor up to 12 months) with an authorized dealer (BSP, SCB or NBS) supported by underlying trade exposure and CBS documentation
USD/WST non-deliverable forward (NDF) executed offshore through a non-resident derivatives dealer or international bank licensed in Samoa, permitted for ICs with USD revenue and WST cost obligations
USD/AUD or USD/NZD cross-currency swaps contractually linked to trade payables or receivables, subject to CBS capital-account reporting and IC exemption filing
Plain-vanilla USD/WST European-style FX options with tenor matching the receivables cycle, permissible only where the nominal amount does not exceed the bank-verified open trade exposure
Natural multi-currency hedging through the IC's USD operational account structure, with prohibition on speculative uncovered positions unless prior written CBS hedging approval is obtained

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of the company's incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a penalty of 10% of the annual government fee; continual default for 90 days after final notice leads to administrative strike-off and dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable on or before each anniversary of incorporation; commonly submitted with the Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to pay by the anniversary date accrues interest at statutory rate; after three months of non-payment the Registrar may strike the company off the International Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certification of Registered Office and Registered Agent Continuity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies via licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the incorporation anniversary, together with the Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Lapse of registered agent/office details for more than 30 days exposes the company to service of process issues, a compliance default notice, and possible strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a standard tax-exempt Samoa International Company under the International Companies Act 1987, unless shareholder resolutions or bank/lender covenants require one; audit becomes mandatory only if the company holds a local business licence or is treated as a resident commercial entity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: If accounts are prepared (statutory or voluntarily), they must be prepared under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or Samoa equivalent generally accepted accounting practice.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must hold current beneficial ownership information. An annual confirmation is submitted with the Annual Return declaring all shareholding transfers made during the preceding 12 months; any transfer after submission must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the next annual confirmation. Failure to disclose a reportable transfer constitutes an offence under the International Companies Act and anti-money laundering regulations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Directors' and Members' Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required by statute; if voluntarily engaged, USD 1,500 - 3,000 for a small trading entity under IFRS

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption under the International Companies Act 1987; no Samoan corporate income tax is payable by an International Company (IC). The entity pays only annual government registration and license fees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No Samoa income tax return applies to an International Company. An annual corporate return must be filed with the Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) through the Companies Online Registration System, using the International Company Annual Return form (IC-AR).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Must be filed within 60 days after the Annual General Meeting, or within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation if no AGM is held. In all cases the filing must be completed no later than 31 December of each calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name and IC registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name and number appearing on the Certificate of Incorporation; no translation is required.
Provide the physical address of the registered agent in Samoa; a P.O. Box alone is not sufficient.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and addresses of all directors and the secretary
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Full names, nationality, and residential addresses of each non-resident director must be listed; Samoa does not require a director to be resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholder schedule and share capital structure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List registered shareholders, class of shares, and aggregate holdings. Beneficial ownership information may be separately declared.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of tax-exempt international company status and economic substance statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the company has not engaged in prohibited local business in Samoa and, if carrying on a relevant activity under Samoa ESR, describe the core income-generating activities performed in Samoa.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties under the International Companies Act: a fixed fine of up to WST 2,000 for each month of default, suspension of the certificate of incorporation, and potential strike-off of the company. The court may additionally impose a fine up to WST 100,000 for non-compliance with annual return obligations.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends, distributions, and deemed distributions made by an International Company to its members. For reference, the standard Samoan statutory rate for a resident non-IC company is 15% on dividends paid to non-residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No treaty relief is needed for IC dividend distributions because the statutory rate is already zero. In the event a payment falls outside the IC exemption, treaty relief would require the beneficial owner to obtain a Samoa Tax Resident Certificate (TRC) from Samoa Revenue Authority and submit a treaty claim form to the payer before the payment date. Samoa's limited double tax treaty network has effectively no application to International Companies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and interest paid by an International Company to non-residents: 0% withholding tax. If paid by a domestic Samoan resident company, the standard domestic WHT rates are 15% for royalties and 15% for interest. No Samoan WHT is imposed on IC outbound service fees.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: None – Samoa has not enacted general transfer pricing documentation rules or local-currency thresholds. International Companies must nevertheless maintain contemporaneous records supporting arm's length pricing for any related-party transactions, especially where the Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply. Standard arm's length principles are expected by the Samoa Revenue Authority for domestic and cross-border dealings.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa's Economic Substance Regulations 2019 apply to International Companies. An IC conducting a relevant activity (banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, financing and leasing, headquarters, holding company, intellectual property, distribution and service centre) must demonstrate economic substance in Samoa by performing core income-generating activities there, maintaining adequate employees and premises, and filing an annual economic substance return with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour. The manufacturing and online sale of wooden Montessori toys may trigger the distribution and service centre category if purchasing and reselling through e-commerce platforms.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Exploiting the International Company exemption to conceal taxable Samoan-source profits from a functional business carried on with Samoan residents, or filing false declarations in the annual return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act 2015 and International Companies Act 1987: fines up to WST 500,000, payment of all evaded taxes and penalties, deregistration of the IC, and forfeiture of the corporate benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for resulting restitution; criminal conviction can lead to imprisonment up to 10 years and a travel ban preventing departure from Samoa pending investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an International Company with no physical presence, no employees, no local records, and no economic substance while undertaking relevant activities such as e-commerce distribution and service provision.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Economic Substance Regulations 2019: administrative penalties up to WST 100,000 per failure; mandatory strike-off; the company's name may be published as non-compliant and the IC certificate may be cancelled.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be fined personally up to WST 50,000 and disqualified from being directors of any Samoan company; repeated non-compliance can trigger criminal liability and a prohibition on re-entry to Samoa for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the IC banking structure to process Amazon Pay and Stripe settlement proceeds without adequate anti-money laundering controls, or failing to identify beneficial owners when rapid digital sales create a high-volume flow of cross-border payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007: fines up to WST 1,000,000 for the entity, forfeiture of assets connected to the violation, and suspension of the company's financial license or bank account access.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be criminally prosecuted with imprisonment up to 14 years for willful money laundering; personal bank guarantees may be called; directors are subject to international travel restrictions and extradition risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: An International Company carrying on trade or business directly with Samoan residents without a valid international company license, or failing to disclose the actual commercial e-commerce activity in the annual return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Companies Act 1987: fines up to WST 250,000, revocation of the IC exemption, and an order to repatriate all prohibited profits to Samoa for potential income tax assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorized prohibited local trade are personally liable for the repatriated profits and statutory damages; the Samoan High Court may impose a personal financial penalty and a travel ban until all amounts are paid.
